tweets.text:
Is $VUZI the newest micro-cap optical play?

They are a smart-glasses company that have started shipping evaluation samples of an optical interconnect that can route up to 19,200 separate light paths across a distance of roughly 30mm. 

We know that as chips become more powerful, the electrical connections moving data around them have to run faster, which increases power consumption and heat.

This is why the industry will be moving optical connections closer to the chips through architectures like NPO, CPO and eventually optical I/O.

Vuzix’s approach spreads the data across thousands of light paths inside a thin waveguide. 

This is very early but they seem to be aggressively going after NPO and CPO.

It is a pretty wild crossover, but there is a technical connection here. 

Vuzix has spent nearly 20 years designing waveguides and developing nanoimprint manufacturing to replicate extremely small optical structures at volume. The original application was smart glasses, while that ability to precisely route light at scale could also have a use inside AI infrastructure.

This is what they claim:

"As AI systems continue to scale, bandwidth is increasingly achieved through parallelism rather than speed alone. Traditional SerDes architectures push a small number of electrical lanes toward their physical limits, while waveguide-based optical architectures enable thousands of parallel channels that dramatically increase aggregate bandwidth, scalability, and energy efficiency."

Will be keeping an eye on it! I just came across this news yesterday.

Data Center Interconnect Data Points
$NOK $CIEN $MRVL $LITE $COHR $CSCO $ANET 

I have been talking a lot about scale-across and the fact that AI clusters are increasingly going to spread across separate buildings, campuses and regions.

Dell’Oro just gave us some nice data points

> Optical transport equipment grew 15% YoY during Q2, 

>Data-center interconnect revenue grew 45% 

> Disaggregated optical line systems grew 80%. 

>Cloud providers now represent 34% of the entire optical transport market.

Data-center interconnect (DCI) is basically the optical network connecting separate data centers. 

If an AI cluster gets too large to fit inside one building, or power availability forces the GPUs to be installed across several locations, those sites still need to exchange enormous amounts of data and operate as one larger system (scale across)

That extends the optical opportunity beyond the short links inside the building and into the coherent equipment carrying data across kilometers.

$CIEN and $NOK are currently the leading vendors in disaggregated optical line systems, so this is a very direct readthrough for both.

tweets.text:
$SMTC  Man, this was a REALLY strong print / guide. 

$341.9M rev vs $328M guide, $0.71 EPS vs $0.61, and Data Center finally broke the $100M level I wanted.

But the forward commentary got me stoked. 

DC went:

Q1: $71.6M
Q2: $100M
Q3 guide: ~$145M
That is +45% sequential next quarter and ~160% YoY.
And they said their FY27 Data Center target is already fully booked, while FY28 is already “over 70% there.”

Then 1.6T qualified EARLIER than management expected. They were being conservative because qualification timing is unpredictable, and now customers basically “want parts tomorrow.” Q3 should be the first meaningful 1.6T quarter.

FiberEdge share is another one. They were ~18% at 800G two years ago. Now they are above 50%, designed into every major module provider they target, sole sourced in several, and expect 1.6T share to exceed 50% by FY-end.

NPO was exactly what I wanted to hear too. They are now involved in roughly 10-15 programs across module makers and are expanding beyond just TIAs/drivers into a more complete solution.

HieFo gain chips are shipping in volume, the original 3 anchor customers are increasing demand, and new customers are coming in.

CopperEdge 1.6T volume deployment with the lead hyperscaler starts in Q4, while several onboard/active-backplane programs are apparently getting close to the finish line.

Then the margins...

Q3 adjusted GM guide is 58.3%.

Excluding the cellular business they just sold: 63.9%.

I think $500M of FY27 Data Center revenue is very achievable now. That would require ~$164M in Q4 after the ~$145M Q3 guide.

And the crazy part is I still think we are early in the 2027 inflection I’ve been waiting for.

This quarter basically strengthened every important part of my thesis.

tweets.text:
$AAOI has been extremely clear and consistent for months that this ramp would require a ton of capital, and that equity would be part of the funding plan.

Feb. 26 10-K: Said substantial capital would be required to expand manufacturing capacity and fund working capital for anticipated growth. Equity was explicitly listed as a funding source.

May 7 10-Q: “Should additional liquidity be needed, our Board may authorize issuance of additional common stock under an at-the-market offering in the future.”

May 7 earnings call: Said the 400G/800G/1.6T capacity investments would be funded through cash, operating cash flow, “some equity sales” and additional debt.

May 13 Needham: CFO Stefan Murry said AAOI had been raising money to make these investments, further expansion would require additional capital, and “the equity markets are always available for us.”

AAOI made $565.5M of capital investments in Q2 alone, including $280M of equipment prepayments, primarily for 400G/800G/1.6T manufacturing capacity.

“We expect CapEx intensity in the second half of the year will be higher than in the first half.”

They would fund it through:

Cash on hand
Operating cash flow
“Some equity sales”
Additional debt

The Aug. 6 10-Q then AGAIN said another ATM could be authorized if additional liquidity was needed.

And then came Rosenblatt on Aug. 18, just THREE DAYS before this new ATM.

2H26 CapEx will be at least as large as 1H26.

The vast majority is going directly into production equipment, machinery and real estate to add capacity.

Management says these investments currently have roughly 9–10 month ROIs.

Asked whether they would keep making similar investments into 2027 if demand remains strong: “Why wouldn’t we?”

Asked how they fund it: “Obviously, right now we’ve been leaning on equity.”

Murry then laid out the longer-term funding mix:

Operating cash flow
Customer contributions
Debt
Potential government support
Equity becoming a smaller piece over time

AAOI says capacity is the constraint. Demand is already far beyond what they can currently supply.

He said credible demand indications from customers are much larger than AAOI expects to be able to produce anytime soon, and that failing to invest aggressively enough could leave AAOI too small to remain relevant with these customers.

Then three days later, $600M ATM.

And today's prospectus STILL leaves future equity financing on the table beyond this facility.

So yes, you can dislike the dilution.

You can think that an ATM is the wrong way to go about it.

Let's talk about LTA's / pricing for Photonics
$LITE $AAOI $GLW $COHR etc. 

Historically a lot of this business was pretty tactical. Customers bought quarter to quarter, suppliers fought for share, and price-downs were part of the game. 

This is not the case anymore due to the supply being this scarce.

$LITE :  Mgmt said they basically never used to have LTAs like this. Now all of their EML capacity is spoken for through 2027, and customers that commit get supply priority. They also said LTAs have helped pricing because they no longer have the same quarterly negotiations for price cuts.

“If anything, prices are holding or they’re increasing.”

And when customers come back asking for MORE capacity than they originally contracted that opens the door for another pricing discussion.

$COHR :

Their LTAs can include

> multi-year volume commitments
> pricing commitments
> minimum demand guarantees
> take-or-pay structures

And many of these agreements extend through the end of the decade.

$GLW:

Says essentially every major optical capacity expansion is now backed by these kinds of LTA's, and eventually they expect this structure to represent the “lion’s share” of the optical business.

So this landscape is increasingly becoming:

Customer commits volume → supplier builds capacity → supply gets reserved → pricing gets protected.

There have been a bunch of $NOK signals recently 

And I want to put them together for you all

Bookmark & share if you find it valuable please! 

The first one came from listening to $FN convo with Rosenblatt. Nok is now 11% of FN’s entire revenue, even though FN said Nokia historically wasn’t a major direct customer. Now FN is telling us the Infinera business is rising, Nokia business is going “very strong,” they’re starting to win incremental Nokia programs and see a “huge amount of potential” to keep expanding the relationship. That is really strong outside validation that the Infinera acquisition is scaling significantly.

Then you have the Scale-Across insight I discussed the other day. 650 Group sees this becoming a >$100B opportunity by early next decade, with roughly 30% tied to 100km+ links. That distance piece is especially interesting for Nokia because as these AI campuses spread farther apart, you increasingly need more of the network stack. IP routing, coherent optics, optical line systems, amplification, etc. Nokia has its hand in all of it.

Then JPM came out and basically said the order book is pointing toward 2027/2028 earnings that consensus still isn’t properly modeling. I think this gets at something I’ve been thinking about for a while. And I wrote a full article dedicated to how I value Nokia and why it's disconnected from consensus. It is genuinely difficult for analysts to model the magnitude of growth that could be coming when so many pieces are inflecting at once.

Infinera is scaling. Optical capacity is expanding. AI + Cloud orders are piling up. IP is becoming another growth engine. Scale-Across is opening a massive new pool of spending. And then you have synergies and operating leverage underneath all of it. Analysts can move estimates higher quarter by quarter, but the actual growth curve could end up being much more nonlinear than that. I think that is why consensus may spend a while chasing Nokia’s earnings power higher.

Then $ADTN , one of Nokia’s competitors, were basically asked whether European Access is transitioning from Huawei + Nokia toward Nokia + ADTRAN as Huawei gets removed, and Tom Stanton essentially agreed. So now you have a competitor openly validating Nokia as one of the main Western beneficiaries of Huawei displacement.

Which leads into the geopolitical side of the story that has been growing some steam, at least on X, as of late. 

The U.S. DFC is essentially the government’s international investment arm, with roughly $205B of investment capacity that can be used to finance strategic infrastructure around the world. Its CEO Ben Black was recently in Helsinki meeting with Nokia leadership, while DFC has been increasingly focused on financing trusted Western AI + telecom infrastructure.

China has used financing for years to help push Huawei infrastructure around the world. The U.S. now has a vehicle that can help finance the Western alternative, and Nokia is one of the few companies capable of supplying such a large portion of that stack.

At the same time, Nokia is reportedly closing almost all of its mainland China sites by the end of 2026 after years of that business shrinking. So Nok is becoming less exposed to China while becoming increasingly important to Western infrastructure.

And of course NVIDIA already put $1B directly into Nokia and is working with them across AI-RAN, with potential opportunities around switching and optics as well.

Do with all of this what you will!

They also called NPO a sticky business because these products are difficult to manufacture.

So if NPO/CPO becomes a meaningful part of the mix, the $FN story is more than rev growth. 

We are looking at a mix of more revenue, higher margins and stickier customer relationships.

The part of the $ADTN thesis I think is important to know...

is how little has to change for the earnings profile to look completely different.

Q2 was:

$281M revenue
40.7% gross margin
3.8% operating margin

Management has said that around $310-$320M of quarterly revenue + 42-43% gross margins, ADTN should be capable of roughly a 10% operating margin.

That is only ~$30-40M more quarterly revenue.

And to me, the path there is pretty visible.

The fastest-growing part of the business is optical, already 39% of revenue and up 13% QoQ last quarter.

But Q2 actually had a BAD mix for margins.

Demand was strongest for lower-margin pluggables, while the higher-margin optical systems were the products being held back by component shortages.

So supply relief can potentially do two things at once:

1 - Unlock more revenue.
2 - Improve the product mix.

That is where the inflection can come in. 

At $320M revenue and a 42.5% gross margin, the math gets you to roughly $32M of quarterly operating income vs ~$11M in Q2.

Essentially a ~14% revenue increase could potentially triple operating income if margins normalize with it.

And this is BEFORE the newer products really matter.

MicroMux trials broaden late 2026 / early 2027.

LiteWave800 opens an entirely new intra-data-center market later.

So I don’t think the $ADTN inflection requires some massive change. 

The current business just needs to convert the demand it already has into a better revenue + margin mix.

My TLDR $ADTN thesis ... 

I think the market is valuing them incorrectly. 

I believe they can re-rate if they execute on the opportunity in front of them.

Optical is already 39% of revenue, grew 22% YoY / 13% QoQ, and hyperscaler revenue grew 97% YoY, mainly from DCI.

They already sell the coherent optics + optical systems used to connect data centers over distance, and there are more products coming down the line. 

MicroMux Quattro should start trials around late 2026 / early 2027. It lets one 400G router port break into four 100G connections, and ADTN says multiple customers, including hyperscalers, are already interested.

LiteWave800 takes ADTN from BETWEEN data centers to INSIDE them for the first time, with trials targeted around Q2 2027 and production later in 2027 / early 2028.

Current demand already exceeds what they can ship.

The higher-margin optical systems were especially supply constrained last quarter, so more component availability could unlock both revenue and margin.

Then add the European Huawei replacement opportunity, which management estimates at >$10B across the markets ADTN serves.

Of course there are risks and ugliness or else it wouldn't be valued the way it is. Some of the biggest ones I see are:

> Supply staying tight.
> The delayed customer slips again.
> Margins next inflect 
> MicroMux / LiteWave take longer to ramp.
> Hyperscaler spending cools 

And the balance sheet still has some ugliness between the 2030 converts and the remaining ADTRAN Networks minority obligation.

But at roughly 0.7x FY26 EV/Sales in my model, I think the setup is interesting.

TLDR:

The bet is that optical keeps becoming a bigger piece of ADTN, AI/DCI keeps pulling demand, new products widen the TAM, supply improves...

and the market eventually starts valuing the business for what it is becoming instead of what it used to be.

Check out the full quoted post for the full write up. 

Not financial advice or a recommendation. DYOR. I own shares.

This is a really big deal..
$CIEN $NOK $ADTN $LITE $COHR 

$100B+ scale-across estimate 

DCI ports going from <1M today to 20-40M by the end of the decade.

And ~30% of the market could be tied to links stretching 100km+.

That means two things happen at once:

1 - Way more connections between AI data centers.
2 - Way more equipment gets pulled into each connection as those distances grow.

$CIEN : Once you get beyond ~40km, DCI increasingly moves toward coherent optics.

As those links stretch toward 100km+ and beyond, amplification and optical line systems become increasingly important. Ciena sells all of that.

And they specifically said the photonics content on a 1,000km scale-across link could be 4-5x the photonics content on a 100km link.

$NOK : The 100km+ piece gets even more interesting because 650 sees these longer networks increasingly pulling in Layer 3 routing as well.

Nokia sells the coherent optics, amplification and optical systems, and the routers.

So we're looking at benefits for both Optical Networks and IP Networks.

$ADTN : the distance breakdown lines up extremely well with what they already sell too.

As DCI moves toward coherent at longer reaches, ADTN sells the coherent optics.

As links get longer and need more optical infrastructure, ADTN sells the line systems and amplification around them.

And as DCI port counts explode, they are also rolling out a product that can take one 400G router port and break it into four 100G ports, with multiple hyperscalers already interested.

And we already talked about the upstream impacts...

$LITE : coherent systems pull demand for narrow-linewidth lasers. Longer amplified routes pull demand for pump lasers. Management says these scale-across components are already effectively sold out.

$COHR : gets paid at multiple points in the network through ZR/ZR+ optics, pump lasers, amplifiers, line cards and even full systems. Communications grew 56% YoY, driven by strength in DCI, scale-across and telecom, and management said demand keeps increasing across DCI / scale-across products.

We're looking at a massive physical buildout here folks. 

Buckle up! It's more than CPO.
